rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for multimodal performance. This config tests the simplest multimodal setup (concatenation fusion, no aggregation) with standard encoders (pca_n2000 for RNA, resnet50 for images) on singleprofile data. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modal baselines and identifies key components to explore further.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieves 52.7% accuracy. This experiment tests weighted fusion (config_017) with the same RNA and image encoders, isolating the effect of fusion method. It balances exploitation (building on the multimodal baseline) and exploration (testing a key design choice). Changing fusion method directly addresses uncertainty about its impact, which is critical for improving accuracy without altering other complex components.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the impact of profile settings and aggregation methods. It balances exploration of key design choices (profile/multimodal) while building on prior multimodal success, avoiding redundant changes.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile settings (config_018: 0.618 accuracy) outperform singleprofile models. This experiment tests whether changing fusion from concat to weighted (while keeping avgpool aggregation and resnet50/pca_n2000 encoders) can further improve accuracy. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy in the promising multiprofile space, balancing exploitation of current strengths with targeted exploration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with a more powerful 'imagenet_vit_l' while keeping other parameters identical to isolate the impact of the image encoder choice. This clarifies whether upgrading the image encoder could further improve performance, balancing exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (a more complex method) while maintaining weighted fusion could further improve performance, isolating the effect of aggregation. This balances exploitation of the promising multiprofile direction with exploration of a critical design choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests using a more advanced image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and transformer aggregation while retaining weighted fusion, isolating the impact of these changes on performance. It balances exploration of stronger image features with the proven effectiveness of weighted fusion, leveraging prior success while addressing potential limitations of resnet50.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019: 0.639) outperform others. This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 RNA encoder with scvi_n200 (config_031) to isolate the impact of RNA representation on performance. It balances exploration (testing a new RNA encoder) and exploitation (building on the successful multiprofile/weighted fusion setup), directly addressing a key design choice with minimal changes.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (config_031) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping scvi_n200 RNA encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. This clarifies whether upgrading the image encoder further improves performance, directly addressing the potential of stronger visual representations in multimodal settings.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion achieve the highest accuracy (0.706245). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with weighted fusion, isolating the effect of aggregation method on performance. It directly compares transformer aggregation (which may capture more complex interactions) against the current best avgpool aggregation, leveraging the strong prior evidence to exploit promising directions.
